questions.text:
Refer to Text A, '"Giant batmobiles": In search of the manta rays of the Hauraki Gulf', on page 2 of the resource booklet.

How does the writer help us to understand the experience of Manta Watch?
You might consider how they have used:
• mood and purpose
• observations about the environment and manta rays
• ideas about helping to protect animals.

Support your answer with quotes and examples of language features from the text.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identify/describe aspects of the text relevant to the question, explain how one or more aspects create meaning. Merit: Explain how two or more aspects work together to create meaning. Excellence: Explain how aspects have been deliberately used to create meanings and effects relating to the writer's purpose and wider contexts. Ideas might include: mood is excited, fun, positive to inform/persuade about Manta Watch NZ; environment is fragile, threatened, vulnerable, rays are mysterious and precious (metaphor, simile, alliteration); citizen science is fun, educational, rewarding, unites people to protect nature.

questions.text:
Refer to Text B, "bush houses", on page 3 of the resource booklet.

How does the writer help us to understand the experience of building a bush house? You might consider how they have used:
• mood and purpose
• descriptions of nature
• ideas about working together
• contrasting attitudes.

Support your answer with quotes and examples of language features from the text.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identify/describe aspects, explain how one or more create meaning. Merit: Explain how two or more aspects work together. Excellence: Explain deliberate use to create meanings relating to purpose and wider contexts. Ideas might include: mood is nostalgic, reflective, positive for sharing memories/experiences (tense, vivid verbs); nature provides shelter, is a playground, hostile but can be tamed (adjectives, comparison, metaphor); teamwork, hard work, persistence pays off, imagination is powerful (pronouns, lack of punctuation); contrast between city/country, nature/human, adult/child (nouns, adjectives, alliteration).

questions.text:
Refer to Text C, "Dad and the camera", on page 4 of the resource booklet.

How does the writer help us to understand their father? You might consider how they have used:
• language to describe their father
• ideas about their relationship with their father
• ideas about special objects.

Support your answer with quotes and examples of language features from the text.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identify/describe aspects, explain how one or more create meaning. Merit: Explain how two or more aspects work together. Excellence: Explain deliberate use to create meanings relating to purpose and wider contexts. Ideas might include: Dad is quiet, reserved, introverted, shy, thoughtful, kind, observant, shows empathy through watching and taking photos (simile, short sentence, symbol, verbs, contrast); relationship was closer than realised, he communicated differently, she liked how he was different, validation means a lot (symbol, point of view, narrative structure); gifts/photographs are precious, can trigger memories, link to the past, have lasting impact (adjectives, alliteration, short sentence, symbol).
